selection: Lowest validation finite Huber plus candidate soft-rank CE, equally averaging predeclared validation cohorts; no test checkpoint selection.
scope: Independent Q(S), Q(G); exact complete goals only; no oracle in inference features, no pruning, no search, no LLM retraining.
hypothesis: Single readout-metric control against the original from-scratch128D Linf baseline. Same neural initialization, raw independent state inputs, fixed exact data and splits, source/goal sampling, losses, budget and unweighted validation selector. A finite offline witness shows more than128 incompatible tight Linf pairs; it proves an exact-representation obstruction but not an average-error bound or greedy impossibility. Reuse existing max_l1 readout: maximum over16 sums of8 absolute coordinate differences. No inference search or oracle features. The changed metric also changes initial distance and gradient scale, so any gain cannot be attributed solely to representational capacity.
